Rashi on Sotah 19a:10:1.hebrew: משלמים - מתנופת חזה ושוק, ואימורין דשלמים:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:10:1.english: From peace-offerings - From the waving of the breast and thigh, and the sacrificial portions (emurim) of the peace-offerings.

Rashi on Sotah 19a:10:2.hebrew: ידיו תביאנה - בבעלים כתיב, וגבי תנופה כתיב:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:10:2.english: "His hands shall bring it" - [This] is written regarding the owners, and it is written regarding waving.

Rashi on Sotah 19a:11:1.hebrew: מה כאן כהן - בסוטה כתיב כהן בתנופת מנחתה:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:11:1.english: Just as here [it is] a Kohen - In the case of a sotah, it is written "the Kohen" with regard to the waving of her meal-offering.

Rashi on Sotah 19a:12:1.hebrew: הא אקרבה - קודם השקאה, דקתני קמץ והקטיר, והדר תניא היה משקה:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:12:1.english: Behold, it was offered - Before the giving to drink, as [the mishnah] teaches "he took a handful and burned [it]," and afterward it teaches "he would give her to drink."

Rashi on Sotah 19a:13:1.hebrew: הכי קאמר כו' - הא דתנא רישא הניף והגיש קמץ והקטיר, לאו דוקא קודם השקאה נקט, ולא איירי בהשקאה כלל, אלא איירי בסדר הקרבת מנחת סוטה, שכן הוא: תנופה, והגשה, קמיצה, והקטרה. והכי קאמר: כשבא להקריבה, היה נוטלה מתוך כפיפה כו'. והדר איירי מי קודם, או השקאה קודם כל אלה, או אם כל אלה קודמין להשקאה, ופליגי בה רבי שמעון ורבנן:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:13:1.english: This is what it is saying, etc. - That which the first clause taught, "he waved it, brought it near, took a handful, and burned it," it did not state [this] specifically as before the giving to drink, and it is not discussing the giving to drink at all. Rather, it is discussing the order of offering the meal-offering of a sotah, for that is the order: waving, bringing near, taking a handful, and burning. And this is what it is saying: when he came to offer it, he would take it out of the basket, etc. And afterward it discusses which comes first — whether the giving to drink [comes] before all of these, or whether all of these precede the giving to drink — and Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis disagree about it.

Rashi on Sotah 19a:1:1.hebrew: דכתיב זאת - ומסתברא, דהא מיהת קממעט, שלא יקנא לה בעל זה פעם אחרת:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:1:1.english: As it is written, "This" - And it is reasonable [to explain it this way], for this much at least it excludes: that this husband may not warn her again another time.

Rashi on Sotah 19a:1:2.hebrew: שני אנשים ושני בועלים - לאחר שהשקה, זה מת, ונישאת לאחר, וקינא לה מבועל אחר:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:1:2.english: Two men and two paramours - After he gave her to drink, this [husband] died, and she married another, and he warned her about a different paramour.

Rashi on Sotah 19a:1:3.hebrew: דכתיב תורת - והא מיהת אתא לרבויי:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:1:3.english: As it is written, "the law of" - And this, at any rate, comes to include.

Rashi on Sotah 19a:5:1.hebrew: ור' יהודה - סבירא ליה וכו'. דאחר שריבה הכתוב ומיעט, ולא פירש מה ריבה ומה מיעט, על כרחך לא מסרן הכתוב אלא לחכמים, לפרש לך לפי חכמתם מה ריבה ומה מיעט. ומסתברא דריבויא אשני אנשים קאי, ואפילו בבועל אחד, ולא אשני בועלים ובעל אחד: כיון דקינא לה כבר ונמצאת נקיה, נראה הדבר שאדם קנטרן הוא ומתכוין להקניטה. הילכך לא שנא מחשד ראשון ולא שנא מאחר:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:5:1.english: And Rabbi Yehuda - holds, etc. For after the verse included and excluded, and did not explain what it included and what it excluded, you must conclude that the verse entrusted them only to the Sages, to explain to you, according to their wisdom, what it included and what it excluded. And it is reasonable that the inclusion applies to two husbands, even with a single paramour, and not to two paramours and one husband: since he already warned her and she was found innocent, it appears that he is a quarrelsome man and intends to provoke her. Therefore, it makes no difference whether it is the first suspicion or another one.

Rashi on Sotah 19a:7:1.hebrew: היה נוטל את מנחתה - הבעל. דהא אמרינן דאין מצות כהונה במנחות אלא מקמיצה ואילך, והגשה נמי תחילת קמיצה היא, שאין זר קרב למזבח. אבל קידוש כלי ויציקה ובלילה, שטעונות שמן, כשר בזר:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:7:1.english: He would take her meal-offering - the husband. For we have stated that the commandment of priesthood in meal-offerings applies only from the kemitza (taking of the handful) onward, and the presentation (hagasha) is also the beginning of the kemitza, since a non-priest may not approach the altar. But the sanctifying of the vessel, the pouring [of oil], and the mixing, which are required for [meal-offerings] that require oil, are valid when performed by a non-priest:

Rashi on Sotah 19a:7:2.english: And he places it on her hand - In order to wave it.

Rashi on Sotah 19a:7:3.hebrew: וכהן מניח ידו מתחתיה - ובגמרא יליף דתנופה צריכי יד בעלים ויד כהן, ובעלים דמנחת סוטה היא האשה:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:7:3.english: And the Kohen places his hand beneath it - And in the Gemara it derives that waving requires the hand of the owner and the hand of the Kohen, and the owner of the Sotah's meal-offering is the woman.

Rashi on Sotah 19a:7:4.hebrew: והגיש - לקרן מערבית דרומית, כדתניא בפרק ג' בסדר מנחות (דף יט:). וכולהו הנך כתיבי במנחת סוטה: תנופה, והקרבה, קמיצה, והקטרה:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:7:4.english: And he brought it near - To the southwestern corner [of the altar], as it is taught in the third chapter of the order of Menachot (19b). And all of these are written with regard to the meal-offering of a sotah: waving, bringing near, taking the handful, and burning.

Rashi on Sotah 19a:7:5.hebrew: והשאר נאכל - שכל הנקמצות שיריהן נאכלין, דכתיב "תורת" בסתם מנחה (ויקרא ו׳:ז׳) "וזאת תורת המנחה כו' עד והנותרת ממנה וגו'":
Rashi on Sotah 19a:7:5.english: And the remainder is eaten - For all [meal-offerings] from which a handful is taken, their remainders are eaten, as it is written "the law of" regarding a meal-offering without specification (Leviticus 6:7): "And this is the law of the meal-offering, etc." until "And the remainder of it, etc."

Rashi on Sotah 19a:8:1.hebrew: ואח"כ מקריב - בגמרא פריך: הא תנא ליה "והקטיר", ומה יקריב עוד לאחר הקטרה?:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:8:1.english: And afterward he sacrifices - In the Gemara it asks: Surely [the Mishnah] already taught "and he burned [it]," so what more would he sacrifice after the burning?

Rashi on Sotah 19a:8:2.hebrew: פלוגתא - דרבנן ור' שמעון, בגמרא ילפינן לה מקראי:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:8:2.english: The dispute - of the Rabbis and Rabbi Shimon, we derive it in the Gemara from verses.

Rashi on Sotah 19a:9:1.hebrew: לר' יאשיה דדריה - אמורא הוא, ובדורו של ר"א בן פדת. ועוד, היה ר' יאשיה שהיה תנא, בר פלוגתא דר' יונתן, בכוליה גמרא. והיינו דקאמר "לר' יאשיה דדריה", דלא תימא לרבי יאשיה הזקן, דלאו אורח ארעא למימרא ליה הכי, שגדול וזקן ממנו היה:
Rashi on Sotah 19a:9:1.english: To R. Yoshiya of his generation - He is an Amora, and [lived] in the generation of R. Elazar ben Pedat. Furthermore, there was [another] R. Yoshiya who was a Tanna, [and was] a disputant of R. Yonatan, throughout the Gemara. And this is why it says "to R. Yoshiya of his generation" — so that you not say [that it refers] to R. Yoshiya the Elder, for it would not be proper [derekh eretz] to speak to him this way, since he was greater and older than [R. Elazar].

Rashi on Sotah 19a:9:2.hebrew: בבעלים מנא לן - שתהא האשה מניפה עם הכהן, דהא קרא בכהן לחודיה כתיב: ולקח הכהן מיד האשה וגו':
Rashi on Sotah 19a:9:2.english: With regard to the owners, from where do we derive [it]? - That the woman should wave together with the priest, for the verse is written only with regard to the priest alone: "And the priest shall take from the woman's hand, etc."

Tosafot on Sotah 19a:7:1.hebrew: היה נוטל - בירושלמי כתיב: "ולקח הכהן מיד האשה את מנחת הקנאות". וכי על ידו הוא מניף, ולא על ידה הוא מניף? אלא מכאן שהוא נוטלה מתוך כלי חול ונותנה בכלי שרת. היינו משמע דלא כפירוש רש"י, דפירש דבעל היה נוטל. ומצינו למימר דקידוש המנחה כשירה בהן. מיהו מצוה בכהן ליטול המנחה מידה, ומאחר שהיה נוטלה, היה נותנה כמו כן לתוך כלי שרת:
Tosafot on Sotah 19a:7:1.english: He would take - In the Yerushalmi it is written: "And the priest shall take from the woman's hand the meal-offering of jealousy." [The Yerushalmi asks:] Is it on his hand that he waves, and not on her hand? Rather, [we learn] from here that he takes it out of a non-sacred vessel and places it in a service vessel. This implies that it is not in accordance with Rashi's explanation, who explained that the husband would take it. And we can say that the sanctification of the meal-offering is valid with them. Nevertheless, it is a mitzvah for the priest to take the meal-offering from her hand, and since he would take it, he would likewise place it into a service vessel:

Tosafot on Sotah 19a:7:2.hebrew: וכהן מניח את ידו תחתיה - האי דאיצטריך תו למיתני "וכהן מניח את ידו תחתיה", ולא קתני בסתם "ומכניס את ידו" — לאשמועינן דתנופה בכהן. ירושלמי: "וכהן מניח את ידו תחתיה" — ואין הדבר כיעור? מניח מפה ואינו חוצץ. מביא כהן זקן; ואפילו תימא כהן ילד, שאין יצר הרע מצויה לשעה. תני ר' חייא: סוטה גידמת, שני כהנים מניפין על ידיה. אבל בגמרא דידן אמרינן בסוף פרק ארוסה (לקמן סוטה דף כז.) דגידמת לא היתה שותה. וי"ל דפליגי אי בעינן קרא כדכתיב:
Tosafot on Sotah 19a:7:2.english: And the priest places his hand beneath it - As for the fact that it was necessary to teach again "and the priest places his hand beneath it," rather than simply teaching "and he inserts his hand" — [this is] to inform us that the waving is done by a priest. Yerushalmi: "And the priest places his hand beneath it" — is the matter not unseemly? He places a cloth, and it does not constitute a barrier. He brings an old priest; and even if you say [he brings] a young priest, [it is no concern,] since the evil inclination is not present for the moment. Rabbi Chiya taught: [In the case of] a sotah whose hands are cut off, two priests wave on her hands. But in our Gemara we say at the end of the chapter "Arusah" (below, Sotah 27a) that a woman whose hands are cut off would not drink. And one can say that they disagree whether we require the verse [to be fulfilled] as it is written.

Tosafot on Sotah 19a:7:3.hebrew: הניף והגיש - בירושלמי יליף הא דאמר בפרק כל המנחות (מנחות דף ס:): "והבאת" — לרבות מנחת העומר להגשה; "והקריבה" — לרבות מנחת סוטה להגשה. וכתיב בתריה: "והרים", והיכן הוא? תנופה כבר קדמה. ומהתם יליף נמי דשיריה נאכלין, דכתיב בתריה: "והנותרת מן המנחה לאהרן" וגו':
Tosafot on Sotah 19a:7:3.english: He waved and brought near - In the Yerushalmi, [the Gemara] derives what it says in the chapter "Kol HaMenachot" (Menachot 60b): "And you shall bring" comes to include the meal-offering of the Omer for the bringing near [to the altar]; "and he shall bring it near" comes to include the meal-offering of a sotah for the bringing near. And it is written after it: "and he shall lift up" — and where is that [lifting]? The waving already preceded it. And from there it also derives that its remainder is eaten, as it is written after it: "And that which is left of the meal-offering shall be Aharon's," etc.
